source_file: Berlin 2026 edition for next app devCon 2026 (flutterCon Berlin), sources listed on the page
question: Q1: Who Is Hiring, Looking, or Worried?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you hire developers or have a say in who gets hired.
sections.hint: Bitkom, Sep 2026: 79,000 unfilled IT jobs in Germany, down from 149,000 in 2023. Start with the hirers: what changed in what they look for, not only in their budget.
no_hands: What do you think hiring managers look for first in a Flutter candidate today?
When did you last see a Flutter role advertised near you, and what did it ask for?
If you were hiring tomorrow with a small budget, would you take a junior or a senior, and why?
hands_up: What are you hiring for right now, and what has changed in the role since last year?
How do you evaluate candidates now that a portfolio can be generated in an afternoon?
Do you hire Flutter-only developers, or Flutter plus native, and why?
What did you stop asking for in interviews this year?
follow_ups: What is the fastest way for someone in this room to stand out to your team?
What is one signal that makes you stop reading a CV?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you are looking for a Flutter job or a Flutter project right now.
sections.hint: Indeed job postings index, Sep 2026: German software-dev postings are at a record low, about half their Feb 2020 level. Let seekers describe the market before anyone gives advice.
no_hands: What would make you start looking: a better offer, a worrying signal at work, or a new technology?
How do you keep an eye on the market while you are not looking?
For those who hire: what would you tell people who are not looking to keep doing anyway?
hands_up: Permanent role, freelance project, or both, and is that by choice?
What gets a reply right now: applications, referrals, open source, or community?
Are you looking only where you live, or across borders and remote too?
How has AI changed the search itself, from screening to take-home tasks?
follow_ups: What advice from the internet turned out to be wrong for your search?
What support from this community would actually help this month?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if this year has made you worry about your own career.
sections.hint: Stack Overflow 2025: 64% of developers say AI is not a threat to their job, 15% say it is; the no camp was 68% a year earlier. Eyes closed, hands up, facilitators count; the closer repeats this.
no_hands: What gives you confidence: your skills, your network, your savings, or your employer?
Is there anything you are quietly watching even though you are not worried?
For the seniors: what did an earlier downturn teach you that applies now?
hands_up: What triggered the worry: fewer job ads, a hiring freeze or cuts close to you, AI demos, or something you would rather keep private?
Is the worry about Flutter specifically, about mobile, or about software careers in general?
What have you actually done about it so far?
follow_ups: What would make the worry go away, and is that within your control?
Who do you talk to about this, and does it help?

wrap_up: Based on the hands in this room, how does the market feel where you live, in one word?
What is one concrete signal a job seeker here should watch this autumn?
